title: Ops rotation retrospective — 2026-10-27
content:
Purpose and audience:
Quick, candid handoff and retrospective for this rotation (10/20–10/27). Intended for SREs, on-call engineers, platform eng partners and observability owners.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Three notable incidents this week: a KV-store latency spike on dedicated-GPU cluster, a cascading retry storm from a misconfigured client release, and intermittent model-routing failures during a canary rollout.
- SLOs: one partial breach on API p95 during the KV latency event; baseline SLOs otherwise stable.
- Follow-ups: short-action items created (JIRA keys listed), need a focused runbook update for KV latency escalation and a failover drill for model routing.

Incident 1 — KV-store latency spike (impact: medium)
- When: 2026-10-22 03:40–04:15 UTC
- Symptom: 95th and 99th percentile latency for dedicated cluster KV operations spiked ~6–8x, causing slow prefix cache reads and elevated request queues in serving runtime.
- Root cause (initial): a nightly compaction job on shard-2 consumed IO burst capacity; compaction paralelled with a snapshot job due to a scheduling regression in the infra cron service.
- Mitigation performed: temporarily paused compaction, promoted a hot-standby leader for shard-2, increased autoscale throttle to shed non-critical background IO.
- Impact: API p95 crossed SLO (target 200ms, observed 420ms) for a 28-minute window; replicating requests saw 5–8% increased tail latency.
- Immediate follow-ups: JIRA-SRE-4123 created to track compaction scheduling fixes + runbook updates. Owner: Liam Chen.

Incident 2 — Downstream retry storm from client release (impact: high but contained)
- When: 2026-10-24 18:10–18:50 UTC
- Symptom: sudden spike in retries from a high-volume customer tenant after a non-idempotent client attempted reconnects; this increased request fanout and saturated request-queue depth on a small pool of dedicated inferencers.
- Mitigation: enabled emergency request rate-limiter for tenant, rolled back routing policy for that tenant to prior stable variant, opened priority channel with customer SE.
- Lessons: need clearer per-tenant circuit-breaker thresholds and a practice run for tenant-level isolation.
- Follow-ups: create tenant-circuit-breaker RFC and add a Canary gating check in product release playbook. Owner: Priya Kapoor.

Incident 3 — Model-routing intermittent failures during canary (impact: low but noisy)
- When: 2026-10-25 09:00–09:35 UTC
- Symptom: 2–3% of canary requests returned 5xx; observed increased fallbacks across regions in the smart router due to a malformed model-variant manifest in the canary bundle.
- Mitigation: disabled canary build, forced routing to last-known-good variant, ran validation job for model manifests.
- Follow-ups: add stricter manifest validation in CI and a pre-rollout synthetic workload test. Owner: Diego Alvarez (infra).

SLO snapshot and notes:
- API generation latency (p95): SLO 99.5% < 200ms. This rotation: 99.33% (partial breach during KV event).
- Overall availability SLI: 99.97% (within target).
- Error budget: remaining 0.24% for quarter — recommend pausing non-urgent risky rollouts until budget recovers.

Operational handoff items (for incoming on-call):
- Active pages and status: none open as of 2026-10-28 08:00 UTC.
- Ongoing tasks to watch:
  1) JIRA-SRE-4123 (KV compaction scheduling) — high priority, blocker for stability improvements.
  2) Tenant circuit-breaker RFC draft in docs repo — needs review from platform-eng.
  3) Canary validation work (manifest schema + synthetic tests) — merged WIP PR, awaiting infra perf tests (link above).
- Known fragile areas: dedicated-GPU shard-2 IO path (follow-up remediation planned), per-tenant routing policy config surface (adds complexity during customer releases).
- Escalation contacts: Diego (infra lead), Priya (platform), SRE manager on-call (pager duty: Emily Zhang).

Action items (clear owners & ETA):
- [ ] Update KV compaction schedule logic and add rate limit guard (Owner: Liam Chen, ETA: 2026-11-03, JIRA-SRE-4123).
- [ ] Draft tenant-level circuit-breaker RFC and demo isolation test harness (Owner: Priya Kapoor, ETA: 2026-11-10).
- [ ] Add manifest schema validation to model-build CI + synthetic canary test (Owner: Diego Alvarez, ETA: 2026-11-05, PR: infra/pull/1876).
- [ ] Run a combined model-routing failover drill with oncall and platform-eng (Owner: Ava Martinez, ETA: 2026-11-09).

Runbook and doc changes needed:
- Add a triage checklist for KV latency spikes (quick checks for compaction vs snapshot jobs, shard leader health, IO saturation metrics).
- Document clear tenant circuit-breaker thresholds and emergency rate-limiter playbook.
- Canary gating: add a quick synthetic smoke test step to the rollout checklist and require manifest-schema pass.

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- Consider exposing a low-effort per-tenant knob that support/SEs can flip to move a tenant to best-effort routing when they cause noisy fanout. Would reduce blast radius for customer-side regressions.
- Investigate whether compaction job can run with IO QoS limits (throttle at OS level) rather than pausing entirely — better for availability.
- Are we confident our autoscale throttle correctly differentiates background IO vs foreground inference traffic? Might be worth a short eng spike.

Meeting cadence & follow-ups:
- Quick sync next Tue (2026-11-02) 10:30 UTC — 15 minutes to review JIRA-SRE-4123 progress and agree on failover drill scope.
- Postmortem-lite for KV event will be drafted after remediation (owner Liam). Aim to publish in Confluence by 2026-11-06.

References / quick links:
- Slack: #sre-oncall, #infra-ops, #platform-release
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/SRE/kv-latency-investigation
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1876
- Related ticket: JIRA-SRE-4123

Quick retrospective (what went well / what to improve):
- Went well: fast triage and clear owner assignments; customer communication channel opened quickly for tenant issue.
- Improve: automated manifest validation earlier would have caught canary issue; better default guardrails for background IO jobs needed.

If you're taking over oncall: read the Action items above, confirm you've subscribed to JIRA-SRE-4123 and check the KV shard-2 dashboards. If anything is unclear ping me (Ava) or drop a note in #sre-oncall.

-- end of notes --
